meta.title: Chinese national congresses
sources: Wikipedia: National People's Congress articles, 1st (1954) to 14th (2023), and the 1st CPPCC of 1949 (composition, infoboxes and leads)

eras.label: The founding conference
eras.blurb: The People's Republic began without any election at all: the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference — delegates invited by the Communist Party — proclaimed the state and acted as its legislature until 1954. It is recorded here as the system's origin, not as a vote.

eras.label: The Mao-era congresses
eras.blurb: The first National People's Congress met in 1954, chosen through tiers of indirect, single-candidate selection under party control. The rhythm soon broke down entirely: the third Congress sat through the Cultural Revolution without meeting for a decade, and the fourth met just once.

eras.label: The reform-era congresses
eras.blurb: Deng Xiaoping's era restored the institution's routine — five-year terms, annual sessions, secret ballots inside the chamber — and the NPC began occasionally registering dissenting votes. The selection of its nearly 3,000 delegates, however, remained a party-managed process from start to finish.

eras.label: The technocratic congresses
eras.blurb: The congresses of the Jiang and Hu years rubber-stamped the market reforms that transformed China, with delegate seats allocated across provinces, the army and the eight licensed minor parties — every one of which formally accepts Communist Party leadership.

eras.label: The Xi-era congresses
eras.blurb: Under Xi Jinping the NPC's residual space narrowed again: the 2018 Congress abolished presidential term limits with two dissenting votes out of nearly three thousand, and the 2023 Congress re-elected Xi unanimously. The theatre of unanimity is itself the message.

elections.label: 1st CPPCC
elections.summary: The 1st National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference was the first meeting of the top political advisory body of the People's Republic of China. It convened in Beijing on 9 October 1949 and ended on 21 December 1954.
elections.caveat: Not an election at all: the delegates were invited by the Communist Party, and the conference proclaimed the People's Republic and acted as its legislature until 1954.

elections.label: 1st NPC

parties.name: Chinese Peasants' and Workers' Democratic Party

elections.summary: The 1st National People's Congress (NPC) was in session from 1954 to 1959. It held four sessions in this period.
elections.caveat: An indirect, Communist Party-controlled selection: delegates are chosen through tiers of party-managed elections with no opposition permitted, and the eight licensed minor parties all formally accept CCP leadership. Recorded here as the workings of a one-party state, not as a competitive election.

elections.label: 4th NPC
elections.summary: The first session passed the 1975 Constitution of the People's Republic of China. The offices of Chairman and Vice Chairman were abolished at the suggestion of Chairman Mao Zedong, passing the role of head of state to the Chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.

elections.summary: The 13th National People's Congress (NPC) was elected from October 2017 to February 2018 and was in session in the five-year period from 2018 to 2023. It held five sessions in this period, occurring around early March every year until before 2023, when the 14th National People's Congress first convened.
elections.caveat: An indirect, Communist Party-controlled selection: delegates are chosen through tiers of party-managed elections with no opposition permitted, and the eight licensed minor parties all formally accept CCP leadership. elections.summary: The 14th National People's Congress (NPC) is the current term of the supreme organ of state power of the People's Republic of China. This term of the National People's Congress convened in Beijing, on 5 March 2023, and is scheduled to continue until March 2028.
elections.caveat: An indirect, Communist Party-controlled selection: delegates are chosen through tiers of party-managed elections with no opposition permitted, and the eight licensed minor parties all formally accept CCP leadership.
